newsitem.title: USA: WellPoint Health buying John Hancock group health units.
newsitem.headline: WellPoint Health buying John Hancock group health units.

text.p: WellPoint Health Networks Inc. said Friday it agreed to buy the group health and related life insurance business of John Hancock Mutual Life Insurance Co. for $86.7 million.

The deal is the second such acquisition this year by Woodland Hills, Calif.-based WellPoint, one of the nation's largest publicly held managed health care companies, which earlier this year purchased the group life and health business of Massachusetts Mutual Life Insurance Co.
The deal is also the latest in a string of acquisitions of insurance businesses by managed care companies.
While the managed care industry has been consolidating for several years, health maintenance organisations have increasingly been buying insurers rather than other HMOs.

"In the past 12 to 18 months, you've seen seven of these acquisitions," said Todd Richter, an analyst with Dean Witter. "The advantage is that buying an insurer is a lot cheaper than buying another HMO."
The cost advantage, he said, reflects the fact that several traditional insurers were shrinking as HMOs grow rapidly and pick up market share from them.
WellPoint said the acquisition of the Hancock business, which currently provides services to about 1.4 million members, will expand its membership to 5.5 million nationwide.

The acquisition also includes Hancock's managed care services subsidiary, Cost Care Inc., WellPoint said. The agreement does not include Hancock's group long-term care business or its unrelated stand-alone group life business.
WellPoint said it was buying the Hancock business as a separate unit and will offer positions to all 2,950 Hancock employees, including some 600 in the greater Boston area.

"This business unit will focus on very large national customers, merging WellPoint's creative managed care model with John Hancock's expertise in servicing these very demanding Fortune 500 customers," the company said.

WellPoint said Hancock's group life and health business, serving some of the largest employers in the nation, has a concentration of business in key geographic areas that are complementary to areas already served by WellPoint.
Nearly two-thirds of Hancock's members are located in California, Texas, Georgia, Ohio, Illinois, Michigan and Massachusetts and the metropolitan areas of the New York City and Washington, D.C.
Cost Care, Hancock's California-based managed care services subsidiary, serves more than 650 clients, providing services to more than 3 million individuals.

Hancock also has nearly 1 million members covered through group life and disability insurance products linked to health coverage, which when combined with WellPoint will result in more than 1.5 million life and disability members.

The acquisition also includes Hancock's estimated 1.3 million dental members, giving WellPoint about 2.8 million dental members -- creating one of the largest dental coverage businesses in the country.
The company said the deal is subject to approval by regulators and was expected to close no later than Jan. 31.
WellPoint stock rose $1 to $32.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
